metadata.name: Product Portal Retail Platform Target Schema
metadata.purpose: Enterprise target data model for multi-tenant SaaS and standalone retail deployments.
metadata.sourceOfTruthPolicy: After approval, Liquibase changelogs remain the executable database source of truth. This JSON remains the architecture and design source.
metadata.compatibility: This is a breaking target redesign of the current Product Portal schema and must not be applied directly to an existing production database.

schemaParityGate.scope: Behavioral and data-model coverage for every business and security capability implemented by the pre-v2 Spring Boot application.
assumptions: There is no production or otherwise valuable data to migrate.
The v2 application and API use UUID identifiers.
Current routes may be retained, but UUID response and path fields require an explicit API version 2.0 contract.
Functional parity preserves behavior and security guarantees; it does not preserve legacy table names or the combined PortalUser persistence model.

decisions.loginIdentifierOwnership: username, email, and phone are optional global authentication identifiers owned by pp_m_identity_account. Every identity must provide at least one identifier; staff and customer profiles do not duplicate identifiers or credentials.
decisions.loginChannelPolicy: The v2 login request carries one generic identifier, password, login context, and organization context when required. Staff use username or email. The primary customer UI uses email or phone. Username remains optional for account-directory lookup and explicitly designated compatibility flows.
decisions.profileActivationVerification: An active platform or organization staff profile requires its identity to have a verified email. An active customer profile requires a verified email or verified phone. The transactional profile-activation service enforces these cross-table rules.
decisions.profileSeparation: platform staff, organization staff, and customers remain composition-based business profiles linked to one identity; JPA entity inheritance is not used.
decisions.sessionAuthorizationContext: pp_t_auth_session binds one authenticated identity to exactly one selected profile type and verifies identity/profile ownership with composite foreign keys. Organization and explicitly selected shop context are persisted when selected.
decisions.shopSelectionPolicy: An organization never supplies an implicit default shop. Organization-level operations may run without shop context; shop-scoped operations require an explicit trusted selector or derive the shop from a server-owned resource such as a cart or order.
decisions.loginThrottling: pp_t_login_throttle_state is a required core authentication table, not an optional supporting table. It throttles every canonical login identifier and trusted source IP without exposing account existence.
decisions.customerAddresses: pp_m_customer_address is a global customer-profile child. A legacy staff identity with saved addresses also receives a customer profile so self-service address behavior remains available. Orders continue to retain immutable address snapshots.
decisions.catalogBrand: pp_m_brand is organization-owned and pp_m_product references it with a tenant-safe composite foreign key.
decisions.productModelNumber: model_number remains a first-class nullable product attribute because it is part of the current product API contract.
decisions.accountDirectoryProjection: The compatibility directory is a read model over identity plus one explicit business-profile context. When an identity owns multiple applicable profiles, profile_type is required; roles from different profile types are never silently merged.
decisions.statusCompatibility: Fixed identity, profile, category, brand, and product lifecycle codes remain application enums protected by check constraints. API adapters may expose display labels. Legacy DELETED values map explicitly to ARCHIVED.
decisions.effectiveProfileStatus: Access is active only when identity, selected profile, and any required organization profile are ACTIVE. The compatibility status precedence is ARCHIVED, SUSPENDED, INACTIVE, PENDING, ACTIVE.

coveredCurrentRoutes.parityRequirement: Classify and normalize one generic global login identifier without account enumeration, enforce distributed identifier and source-IP throttling, verify the credential and selected profile, persist the login attempt, and issue tokens bound to one server-side session and authorization context.
Rotate an opaque refresh token atomically within its family, preserve the session profile and tenant context, detect reuse, and revoke the compromised family.
Revoke the addressed session and refresh-token family idempotently.

Create one identity, one customer profile, the resolved organization customer profile, and the default scoped customer-role assignment in one transaction; reject duplicate normalized identifiers safely and keep the customer profile pending until an email or phone is verified.

Return the compatibility account-directory projection for one explicitly selected profile context, including effective status, organization, active assignments, and customer addresses when authorized.
Return a stable, tenant-safe, paginated account-directory projection filtered by effective status with an allow-listed sort contract.
Return only addresses owned through the authenticated identity's customer profile, ordered with the active default first.
Create an owned address transactionally; the first active address becomes default and at most one active default may exist per customer.
Resolve the address by both UUID and authenticated customer-profile ownership so another account's address is never disclosed.
Return the organization-owned category, parent summary, lifecycle status, and audit metadata without cross-tenant lookup.
Resolve the requested organization-owned category subtree and return a stable paginated product projection including brand and model number.

acceptanceCriteria: Every production-facing current route above has a v2 persistence path and query pattern.
All v2 identifiers are UUIDs; legacy Long identifiers are not silently coerced.
Every tenant-owned read and write includes organization ownership in the predicate or a tenant-safe composite foreign key.
Authentication identifiers and credentials have exactly one authoritative persistence owner.
Refresh rotation, logout, default-address changes, registration, and role assignment are transactionally safe under concurrent requests.
Status filtering uses the documented effective-status precedence and maps legacy DELETED to ARCHIVED.
The account-directory facade requires an explicit profile type when one identity owns more than one applicable business profile.
The schema document passes structural validation for table count, creation order, local columns, foreign-key targets, and referenced unique keys.
Shop-scoped operations fail closed when no explicit or server-derived shop context exists; standalone mode never implies a default shop.

apiCompatibility.identifierChange: All exposed Long identifiers become UUID values.
apiCompatibility.routePolicy: Retain current route semantics where practical; use a compatibility query facade for combined account-directory responses instead of recreating a generic user aggregate.
apiCompatibility.statusPolicy: Return stable status codes. A compatibility response may derive displayName and active metadata from the application enum catalog.

fieldMappings.user.id: Replace the ambiguous legacy id with identityAccountId, profileType, and profileId. profileId identifies the selected business actor and all three values are UUIDs.
fieldMappings.user.usernameEmailPhone: Read nullable global identifiers from pp_m_identity_account only. Username is optional in v2; never return email or phone to an unauthorized directory caller.
fieldMappings.user.fullName: Read from the selected staff profile, or from organization customer display_name_override falling back to customer display_name.
fieldMappings.user.organization: Read from the explicitly selected organization context; platform-staff responses have no implicit organization.
fieldMappings.user.rolesAndAssignments: Read only from the selected profile's currently effective assignments; never union staff and customer roles.
fieldMappings.user.status: Derive from identity, selected profile, and organization-customer profile using the documented effective-status precedence.
fieldMappings.user.addresses: Read from the customer profile owned by the identity and return only when the caller is authorized for self-service address data.
fieldMappings.address.country: The v2 persistence and contract use ISO countryCode; a temporary v1 adapter may resolve a display country string.
fieldMappings.product.name: Map the API name field to pp_m_product.display_name.
fieldMappings.product.skuCode: Map the API skuCode field to pp_m_product.sku.
fieldMappings.product.brandAndModelNumber: Map brand through pp_m_brand and modelNumber through pp_m_product.model_number.

MULTI_TENANT.description: One platform hosts multiple organizations. A request resolves organization and optional shop scope.
organizationResolution: organization slug from a configured subdomain or tenant path
MULTI_TENANT.boundaryRule: When routing and authenticated contexts are both present, their organization identifiers must match. A client-supplied organization identifier never overrides either trusted context.
MULTI_TENANT.authenticatedContextRule: For login without a route selector, authenticated context may be inferred only when the credential resolves to exactly one active organization profile. Ambiguous multi-organization identities and public registration require subdomain, custom-domain, or path resolution.
MULTI_TENANT.shopResolution: An optional explicit X-Shop-ID selector is loaded with both organization_id and shop_id predicates. Cross-organization and inactive shops are treated as unavailable, and no organization default is inferred.
MULTI_TENANT.uiHomeBehavior: Show nearby and favorite shops, then enter a selected shop catalog.

STANDALONE.description: The same schema and application run with one configured organization that may own one or many shops.
STANDALONE.shopResolution: No shop is inferred from standalone configuration. X-Shop-ID is optional for organization-level operations and mandatory for shop-scoped operations until an explicit path, domain, or server-owned-resource selector is implemented.
STANDALONE.uiHomeBehavior: Load active shops. If one shop exists, navigate to its explicit shop route; if multiple shops exist, require a choice and optionally suggest nearest, favorite, or last-used shops.
STANDALONE.rule: Standalone mode is configuration, not a separate schema, and it fixes only the organization boundary.

selectionSources: explicit X-Shop-ID validated against the resolved organization
explicit shop path or server-controlled shop domain when implemented
shop ownership derived from an existing server-owned cart, order, or similar aggregate
shopContextPolicy.missingSelectionRule: Organization-level operations continue without shop context. Shop-scoped operations reject the request with a stable HTTP 400 missing-shop error.
shopContextPolicy.authorizationRule: Shop selection identifies the requested resource scope but never grants access; staff and customer authorization must independently contain that shop.
shopContextPolicy.cacheRule: Public shop catalogs should prefer shop identity in the URL. Header-selected GET responses require an explicit cache key or Vary policy that includes X-Shop-ID.
shopContextPolicy.defaultRule: The platform has no organization-wide default shop and never silently substitutes one.

identityModel.authenticationSubsystem: One application-owned authentication subsystem and token format.

loginRequestContract.identifier: Required generic login value with a maximum accepted length of 254 characters. The authentication service classifies, normalizes, and hashes it exactly once before lookup or throttling.
loginRequestContract.password: Required for the v2 password flow and verified only after identifier and source-IP throttling pass.
loginRequestContract.loginContext: Required explicit value: PLATFORM_STAFF, ORGANIZATION_STAFF, or CUSTOMER. A client may fix this value by application area, but the server must not infer it from a role.
loginRequestContract.organizationContext: Required for ORGANIZATION_STAFF and resolved from a trusted subdomain, custom domain, signed gateway header, or organization code. It is optional for CUSTOMER and forbidden for PLATFORM_STAFF.
loginRequestContract.failureResponse: Unknown, disabled, unverified, profile-mismatch, bad-password, and throttled cases return the same external authentication failure shape and comparable timing.

loginContexts.PLATFORM_STAFF: Platform realm; global identity username or email resolves the identity, which must own an active platform staff profile and have a verified email.
loginContexts.ORGANIZATION_STAFF: Organization realm; global identity username or email plus resolved organization identifies an active organization staff profile whose identity has a verified email.
loginContexts.CUSTOMER: Customer realm; the primary customer UI accepts verified email or verified phone and resolves an active customer profile. Username is not offered by new customer clients and is permitted only by an explicitly designated compatibility endpoint.

identityModel.identityProfileRule: Authentication identifiers, credentials, and global verification exist only in pp_m_identity_account. Staff and customer tables are business profiles or memberships and never contain usernames, passwords, or other login credentials.
identityModel.identifierPresenceRule: Each identity has at least one of username, email, or phone. Each supplied identifier and its normalized companion are stored together, and global uniqueness applies only when an identifier is present.
identityModel.identifierNormalizationRule: Username and email are lowercased and trimmed; phone is canonical E.164. Identifier classification is recorded without the raw value, and HMAC input is identifier_type + ':' + canonical_value so channels cannot collide in security telemetry.
identityModel.profileActivationVerificationRule: Identity activation requires one verified email or phone. Platform and organization staff activation additionally requires verified email; customer activation requires verified email or phone. Enforce profile-specific activation in one transactional application service because it spans identity and profile tables.
identityModel.authorizationSubjectRule: Authentication establishes identity_account_id and one session-bound profile. Authorization evaluates profile_type, profile_id, request organization, and any explicitly selected or server-derived shop. Sessions remain identity-owned, while staff and customer role assignments are profile-owned.
identityModel.profileLifecycleRule: Global identity status and profile status are independent. Disabling one organization membership must not disable another profile owned by the same identity.
identityModel.accountLinkingRule: Never merge records only because normalized identifiers match. Existing identities are linked to new profiles only after ownership verification or an authenticated invitation flow.
identityModel.passwordRule: Store only Argon2id or BCrypt password hashes. Never store plaintext or reversible passwords.
identityModel.sessionRule: Access tokens are short-lived. Server-side session state in pp_t_auth_session binds the selected profile and controls refresh eligibility, revocation, credential-change invalidation, idle timeout, and absolute timeout.
identityModel.refreshTokenRule: Use rotating opaque refresh tokens. Persist only keyed token hashes and rotation state in pp_t_refresh_token_family; never persist or log a bearer token.
identityModel.passwordResetRule: Password reset responses are enumeration-safe. Issue a reset only through a verified email or phone channel, persist only selector and token hashes, enforce single use and short expiry, and revoke all existing sessions after a successful reset.

staffAssignmentStorage.rationale: Platform and organization staff share role, permission, scope, validity, revocation, and audit semantics. Strict profile/scope constraints and profile-specific partial indexes provide correctness and efficient lookup without duplicating authorization infrastructure.
splitTriggers: platform authorization moves to a separately secured service or database
platform and organization assignments develop different lifecycle or approval rules
tenant row-level-security policies become materially simpler with physical separation
measured production query plans demonstrate a partitioning or isolation need that partial indexes cannot address

definition.scope: Where the actor can do it.
definition.assignment: A business profile plus role plus concrete platform, organization, or shop scope.

authorizationEvaluation: Resolve the requested active platform-staff, organization-staff, or customer profile owned by that identity.
Resolve the request organization and any explicit or server-derived shop context.
Load active, currently valid role assignments for the resolved profile.
Reject assignments whose scope does not contain the requested resource.
Authorize only when the required permission code is present.
Write security-sensitive decisions and mutations to pp_a_audit_log.

referenceDataModel.fixedBehavioralCodes: Security-sensitive and code-defined values such as scope types, profile types, authentication methods, and token lifecycle states remain application enums protected by database check constraints.
referenceDataModel.codeRule: Reference status codes are stable external identifiers, are seeded through versioned Liquibase changesets, and are never renamed or physically deleted after use.
referenceDataModel.administrationRule: Tenant and platform administrators cannot create arbitrary canonical workflow states. Deprecation and presentation metadata changes require an approved platform change.
referenceDataModel.transitionRule: Reference-table foreign keys validate current status membership; transactional application state machines validate allowed status transitions and their side effects.
referenceDataModel.presentationRule: APIs expose stable status codes. Web and mobile clients resolve labels from display_name_key and may apply tenant-specific label overrides without changing canonical behavior.

rules: Every organization-owned table carries organization_id, including high-volume transaction tables.
Every tenant query includes organization_id even when filtering by a globally unique UUID.
Composite foreign keys are used where practical to prevent cross-organization relationships.
Shop-scoped records carry both organization_id and shop_id.
Platform operations require an explicit privileged code path and cannot inherit an organization from untrusted input.
PostgreSQL row-level security is recommended as defense in depth after the application access model is stable.

identifierStrategy.fallbackGeneration: PostgreSQL gen_random_uuid() when UUIDv7 generation is not available.
identifierStrategy.exposureRule: UUID primary keys may be exposed by APIs, but authorization must never depend on UUID secrecy.
identifierStrategy.businessIdentifierRule: Business identifiers are separately constrained and never used as mutable primary keys.
identifierStrategy.referenceIdentifierRule: Small, immutable, system-managed reference catalogs use their stable uppercase code as the primary key instead of an unnecessary UUID.

dataStandards.timestamps: TIMESTAMPTZ(6), stored in UTC and converted only at system boundaries.
dataStandards.localBusinessTimes: TIME values are interpreted using pp_m_shop.timezone.
dataStandards.money: NUMERIC(19,4) plus ISO-4217 CHAR(3) currency_code. Never use floating-point types.
dataStandards.username: Optional identity-owned login identifier. Store display value and lowercase trimmed normalized value in pp_m_identity_account. Usernames are globally unique when present and contain only lowercase letters, digits, dots, underscores, and hyphens after normalization.
dataStandards.email: Optional identity-owned login identifier. Store display value and lowercase trimmed normalized value; uniqueness applies when present. Record email_verified_at only for the currently verified value.
dataStandards.phone: Optional identity-owned login identifier. Store canonical E.164; uniqueness applies when present. Record phone_verified_at only for the currently verified value.
dataStandards.loginIdentifier: Classify a submitted generic identifier as USERNAME, EMAIL, PHONE, or UNKNOWN before persistence. Hash the type-prefixed canonical value with an HMAC for throttle and audit storage; never persist or log the submitted value.
dataStandards.json: JSONB is permitted only for flexible metadata and immutable snapshots, not for core relational attributes.
dataStandards.optimisticLocking: Mutable aggregate roots contain version BIGINT and are updated with compare-and-swap semantics.
dataStandards.deletion: Business and security records use lifecycle status or revocation. Hard delete is restricted to safe child data and test environments.
dataStandards.binaryAssets: Store object-storage keys and metadata, not image binary data.
dataStandards.securitySecrets: Persist only keyed hashes of high-entropy refresh and reset tokens. Store cryptographic peppers in a managed secret store, never in the database or source control.

tablePrefixes.pp_t_: Transactional, mapping, assignment, or relationship data.

mutableAudit.name: created_by
mutableAudit.description: Stable actor reference; no polymorphic foreign key.

assignmentLifecycle.name: is_active
assignmentLifecycle.description: False only after explicit revocation. Natural expiration is represented by valid_until while this remains true.

assignmentLifecycle.name: valid_until
assignmentLifecycle.description: Exclusive end of the authorization validity window; null means no scheduled expiry.

assignmentLifecycle.name: revoked_at
assignmentLifecycle.description: Required together with revoked_by and revoked_reason when is_active is false.

tables.name: pp_m_organization
tables.description: Tenant organization. Standalone deployment contains exactly one active organization.

uniqueConstraints.name: uk_pp_m_organization_tenant_key
uniqueConstraints.purpose: Candidate key for tenant-safe references when a business code is required.

tables.deletePolicy: RESTRICT; archive through status_code.
businessRules: organization_code and slug are immutable after external use.
At least one active shop is recommended before an organization is published.
Standalone mode validates that the configured organization exists and is active at application startup.

tables.name: pp_m_shop
tables.description: A physical or virtual retail shop owned by one organization.

uniqueConstraints.name: uk_pp_m_shop_tenant_identity
uniqueConstraints.purpose: Referenced by tenant-safe composite foreign keys.

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_m_shop_coordinates

indexes.name: idx_pp_m_shop_nearby_prefilter
indexes.predicate: status_code = 'ACTIVE' AND latitude IS NOT NULL AND longitude IS NOT NULL
indexes.note: For scale, add PostGIS geography(Point,4326) and a GiST index.

tables.deletePolicy: RESTRICT; close or archive through status_code.
businessRules: A shop belongs to exactly one organization.
Nearby-shop searches include only active shops with complete coordinates.
An organization has no implicit default shop.
Shop-scoped operations require an explicit trusted shop selector or derive shop ownership from a server-owned resource.

tables.name: pp_m_identity_account
tables.description: Global authentication identity and the only owner of credentials, verification, MFA, lock, and session-invalidating state.

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_m_identity_account_normalized_username
checkConstraints.expression: (username IS NULL AND username_normalized IS NULL) OR (username IS NOT NULL AND username_normalized = lower(btrim(username)) AND username_normalized ~ '^[a-z0-9._-]{3,100}$')

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_m_identity_account_normalized_email
checkConstraints.expression: (email IS NULL AND email_normalized IS NULL) OR (email IS NOT NULL AND email_normalized = lower(btrim(email)) AND email_normalized ~ '^[^[:space:]@]+@[^[:space:]@]+$')

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_m_identity_account_identifier_presence
checkConstraints.expression: username_normalized IS NOT NULL OR email_normalized IS NOT NULL OR phone_e164 IS NOT NULL

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_m_identity_account_email_verification
checkConstraints.expression: email_verified_at IS NULL OR email_normalized IS NOT NULL

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_m_identity_account_phone_verification
checkConstraints.expression: phone_verified_at IS NULL OR phone_e164 IS NOT NULL

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_m_identity_account_active_contact_verification
checkConstraints.expression: status_code <> 'ACTIVE' OR email_verified_at IS NOT NULL OR phone_verified_at IS NOT NULL

tables.deletePolicy: Never hard-delete after authentication or profile activity. Disable, revoke sessions, and anonymize identifiers only through an approved privacy workflow.
securityRules: This is the only table that contains password_hash and global credential state.
MFA is mandatory when any active profile receives a privileged role.
Password hashes, submitted credentials, verification state, and authentication responses must never be logged.
Changing credentials_changed_at revokes every session and refresh-token family for this identity.
Tenant administrators cannot enumerate or directly mutate global identity records.

Distributed canonical login-identifier and trusted source-IP failure counters are stored only in pp_t_login_throttle_state; identity locked_until is reserved for explicit account-level security or administrative locks.
An ACTIVE identity has at least one verified email or phone. Activating a staff profile additionally requires verified email and is enforced by the transactional profile-activation service.
businessRules: One identity may own platform-staff, organization-staff, and customer profiles concurrently.
At least one global username, email, or phone identifier is required. Each is optional individually and globally unique when present; they are not organization-level membership attributes.
Username is optional and retained for account-directory lookup and explicitly designated compatibility login flows; new customer clients use email or phone.
Email and phone are accepted as login channels only after their matching verification timestamp is populated.

Changing email or phone clears that channel's verification timestamp in the same identity transaction. If no verified channel remains, the identity transitions to PENDING; staff authentication remains denied until email verification is restored.
Matching identifiers never auto-link identities; linking requires proof of ownership.
Global identity suspension blocks authentication through every profile.

tables.name: pp_t_login_throttle_state
tables.description: Low-latency distributed throttle state for canonical typed login identifiers and trusted source-IP keys.

columns.name: identifier_hash
columns.description: HMAC of identifier_type + ':' + canonical login identifier for LOGIN_IDENTIFIER scope, or of canonical trusted source IP for IP_ADDRESS scope; raw values are not persisted.

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_login_throttle_state_failure_window
checkConstraints.expression: (failed_attempt_count = 0 AND failure_window_started_at IS NULL AND last_failed_at IS NULL AND locked_until IS NULL) OR (failed_attempt_count > 0 AND failure_window_started_at IS NOT NULL AND last_failed_at IS NOT NULL AND last_failed_at >= failure_window_started_at AND (locked_until IS NULL OR locked_until >= last_failed_at))

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_login_throttle_state_success
checkConstraints.expression: last_success_at IS NULL OR last_failed_at IS NULL OR last_success_at <= last_failed_at OR failed_attempt_count = 0

indexes.name: idx_pp_t_login_throttle_state_updated
indexes.note: Supports retention cleanup of inactive throttle rows.

tables.deletePolicy: Purge inactive rows after the configured security-retention window; never use this mutable state as the historical login audit.
securityRules: identifier_hash uses an HMAC key held outside the database. LOGIN_IDENTIFIER hashes include the identifier type prefix so equivalent strings in different channels cannot collide.
Source IP is accepted only from trusted proxy resolution and canonicalized before hashing.
Throttle lookups and updates never reveal whether a matching identity account exists.
The application database role may insert and update throttle state but cannot alter append-only login history.
businessRules: Exactly one row exists per throttle scope and keyed identifier hash.
Failure updates initialize the row idempotently and acquire a row-level write lock before changing counters.
A failure outside the configured window starts a new window; reaching the configured threshold sets locked_until.
Successful authentication clears the matching canonical login-identifier failure state and may clear the trusted source-IP state according to policy.
pp_t_login_attempt remains the authoritative append-only history; this table is only current enforcement state.

tables.name: pp_m_platform_staff_profile
tables.description: Platform-operator business profile, such as SUPER_ADMIN or support personnel, linked one-to-one to a global identity account.
tables.deletePolicy: Never hard-delete after assignment or audit activity; deactivate the profile and revoke its assignments.
securityRules: An active platform profile requires an ACTIVE identity account.
Privileged platform roles require MFA on the linked identity account.
Profile suspension removes platform access without disabling other profiles.
businessRules: An identity has at most one platform staff profile.
The linked identity account owns the global username or email used in the platform login realm and must have a verified email before this profile becomes ACTIVE.
Role assignments reference platform_staff_profile_id, never identity_account_id.

tables.name: pp_m_organization_staff_profile
tables.description: Organization-owned staff membership and business profile linked to a global identity account.
tables.deletePolicy: Never hard-delete after assignment or business activity; deactivate the membership and revoke its role assignments.
businessRules: An identity has at most one staff profile per organization but may belong to multiple organizations.
Organization profile status controls only that membership; identity status controls authentication globally.
home_shop_id is informational and does not grant permissions.
The organization login key is the resolved organization plus the linked identity's global normalized username or email.
Role assignments reference organization_staff_profile_id, never identity_account_id.

tables.name: pp_m_staff_role
tables.description: Built-in or organization-custom staff role.

columns.name: organization_id
columns.description: Null for system roles; populated for organization-custom roles.

uniqueConstraints.name: uk_pp_m_staff_role_id_scope
uniqueConstraints.description: Candidate key used by role assignments to enforce exact role-scope compatibility.

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_m_staff_role_system_owner
checkConstraints.expression: NOT is_system OR organization_id IS NULL

tables.deletePolicy: System roles are immutable. Custom roles may be deactivated only when no active assignment depends on them.
businessRules: Recommended built-in roles are SUPER_ADMIN, ORG_ADMIN, SHOP_MANAGER, and SHOP_USER.
A role's scope_type must match every assignment using that role; the composite assignment foreign key enforces this invariant.
Organization-custom roles cannot grant permissions outside their allowed scope.

tables.name: pp_m_staff_permission
tables.description: System-defined staff permission catalog.
tables.deletePolicy: Seeded permissions are never deleted; deprecate through is_active.
businessRules: Permission codes are API and policy constants and therefore immutable.
Example codes: ORGANIZATION:MANAGE, SHOP:MANAGE, PRODUCT:READ, PRODUCT:WRITE, ORDER:MANAGE.

tables.name: pp_t_staff_role_permission
tables.description: Many-to-many mapping between staff roles and permissions.
tables.deletePolicy: Mappings may be removed, but every change must be audited.
businessRules: Permission minimum scope must be compatible with role scope.
Changes to built-in role mappings require platform-level authorization.

tables.name: pp_t_staff_role_assignment
tables.description: Assigns a staff role to exactly one staff business profile at a concrete scope.
tables.tenantBoundary: organization_id when scope is ORGANIZATION or SHOP

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_staff_role_assignment_exact_profile
checkConstraints.expression: (profile_type = 'PLATFORM_STAFF' AND platform_staff_profile_id IS NOT NULL AND organization_staff_profile_id IS NULL) OR (profile_type = 'ORGANIZATION_STAFF' AND platform_staff_profile_id IS NULL AND organization_staff_profile_id IS NOT NULL AND organization_id IS NOT NULL)

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_staff_role_assignment_scope
checkConstraints.expression: (scope_type = 'PLATFORM' AND organization_id IS NULL AND shop_id IS NULL) OR (scope_type = 'ORGANIZATION' AND organization_id IS NOT NULL AND shop_id IS NULL) OR (scope_type = 'SHOP' AND organization_id IS NOT NULL AND shop_id IS NOT NULL)

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_staff_role_assignment_validity
checkConstraints.expression: valid_until IS NULL OR valid_until > valid_from

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_staff_role_assignment_revocation
checkConstraints.expression: (is_active AND revoked_at IS NULL AND revoked_by IS NULL AND revoked_reason IS NULL) OR (NOT is_active AND revoked_at IS NOT NULL AND revoked_by IS NOT NULL AND revoked_reason IS NOT NULL)

exclusionConstraints.name: ex_pp_t_staff_role_assignment_platform_window
exclusionConstraints.description: Prevents overlapping effective windows for the same platform profile, role, and concrete scope while allowing sequential reassignment.

exclusionConstraints.name: ex_pp_t_staff_role_assignment_org_window
exclusionConstraints.description: Prevents overlapping effective windows for the same organization profile, role, and concrete scope while allowing sequential reassignment.

indexes.name: idx_pp_t_staff_role_assignment_platform_active
indexes.predicate: is_active = true AND profile_type = 'PLATFORM_STAFF' AND platform_staff_profile_id IS NOT NULL

indexes.name: idx_pp_t_staff_role_assignment_org_staff_active
indexes.predicate: is_active = true AND profile_type = 'ORGANIZATION_STAFF' AND organization_staff_profile_id IS NOT NULL

tables.deletePolicy: Assignments are revoked, not deleted.
businessRules: Exactly one staff profile foreign key is populated.
scope_type equals the assigned role scope_type and is enforced by a composite foreign key.
An organization-owned custom role may only be assigned inside its owning organization.
An organization staff profile may never receive PLATFORM scope.
The linked identity account does not receive roles directly.
Natural expiration is evaluated through valid_until while is_active remains true; is_active = false represents an explicit revocation with complete revocation metadata.
Active assignments for the same profile, role, and concrete scope may not have overlapping validity windows; adjacent non-overlapping windows are allowed.
Authorization evaluates is_active and the validity window on every security-sensitive request.

tables.name: pp_m_customer_profile
tables.description: Global customer business profile linked one-to-one to a shared identity account and reusable across organizations.
tables.deletePolicy: Deactivate or anonymize profile fields under an approved privacy workflow; never cascade-delete organization profiles, orders, or audit history.
businessRules: An identity has at most one global customer profile.
A staff-only identity does not require a customer profile.
Joining an organization creates an organization customer profile linked through customer_profile_id.

tables.deletePolicy: Revoke immediately; purge only after the security retention period and after dependent refresh families and login attempts are eligible for purge.
securityRules: Exactly one identity account owns every session.

Access-token validation rejects non-active sessions, expired idle or absolute timeouts, and sessions created before the identity's latest credential change.
The access token profile claims must exactly match the session profile context and are authorized only after confirming that the profile remains active.
Revoking a session also revokes its refresh-token family in the same transaction.
IP and user-agent data are security telemetry with restricted access and explicit retention.
Session identifiers are never treated as authentication secrets.
businessRules: One identity may have multiple concurrent device sessions subject to policy.
A session binds one selected profile but does not own roles; authorization reloads currently effective profile assignments.
Platform-staff sessions are not silently bound to a tenant. Organization support access requires an explicit separately audited request context.
Organization-staff sessions always bind one organization. Customer sessions may be global or start with an optional explicitly selected organization and shop context.
Refresh preserves the session-bound profile context and cannot switch actor type or profile.
last_seen_at and idle_expires_at updates are rate-limited to avoid a database write on every API request.
Standalone and multi-tenant deployments use the same session model.

tables.name: pp_t_refresh_token_family
tables.description: Server-side state for one rotating opaque refresh-token family belonging to an authentication session.

columns.name: family_selector_hash
columns.description: Keyed hash used to locate the family without storing the opaque token selector.

columns.name: current_token_hash
columns.description: Keyed hash of the currently valid high-entropy refresh token.

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_refresh_token_family_expiry
checkConstraints.expression: expires_at > issued_at AND (last_rotated_at IS NULL OR last_rotated_at >= issued_at) AND (last_used_at IS NULL OR last_used_at >= issued_at)

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_refresh_token_family_revocation
checkConstraints.expression: (status_code IN ('ACTIVE','EXPIRED') AND revoked_at IS NULL AND revoked_by IS NULL AND revocation_reason_code IS NULL) OR (status_code IN ('REVOKED','COMPROMISED') AND revoked_at IS NOT NULL AND revoked_by IS NOT NULL AND revocation_reason_code IS NOT NULL)

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_refresh_token_family_reuse
checkConstraints.expression: reuse_detected_at IS NULL OR (status_code = 'COMPROMISED' AND revoked_at IS NOT NULL AND reuse_detected_at >= issued_at)

tables.deletePolicy: Revoke rather than delete; purge only after token expiry and the security investigation retention window.
securityRules: The client receives a high-entropy selector, generation, and secret; the database stores only keyed hashes and the current generation.
The HMAC pepper is versioned and stored in a managed secret store outside the database.
Refresh rotates current_token_hash and current_generation atomically using a row lock or optimistic compare-and-swap.
Presentation of a stale generation is treated as reuse, marks the family and session compromised, and requires reauthentication.
Refresh tokens, selectors, token hashes, and Authorization headers are never logged.
businessRules: Each authentication session has at most one refresh-token family.
A refresh family cannot outlive its parent session absolute expiry.
Revoking either the session or family prevents further refresh.

columns.name: organization_identifier_hash

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_login_attempt_context_scope

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_login_attempt_failure_reason

checkConstraints.expression: (outcome_code = 'SUCCESS' AND failure_reason_code IS NULL AND auth_session_id IS NOT NULL AND identity_account_id IS NOT NULL) OR (outcome_code IN ('FAILED','THROTTLED') AND failure_reason_code IS NOT NULL AND auth_session_id IS NULL)

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_login_attempt_hashes

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_login_attempt_metrics

partitioning.archivePolicy: Drop or archive partitions under an approved security and privacy retention schedule.

tables.deletePolicy: Application roles have no UPDATE or DELETE privilege. A controlled retention process purges complete partitions.
securityRules: Login responses use the same external message and comparable timing for unknown accounts and bad passwords.

source_ip is accepted only from the network layer's trusted proxy resolution.
metadata must not contain credentials, tokens, raw identifiers, or unnecessary PII.

businessRules: Write exactly one final outcome for every login request, including throttled requests.

tables.name: pp_t_password_reset_token
tables.description: Single-use, short-lived password-reset credential represented in storage only by keyed hashes.

columns.name: selector_hash
columns.description: Keyed hash used to locate the row without persisting the token selector.

columns.name: token_hash
columns.description: Keyed hash of the high-entropy reset-token secret.

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_password_reset_token_hashes
checkConstraints.expression: selector_hash ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' AND token_hash ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' AND (user_agent_hash IS NULL OR user_agent_hash ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$')

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_password_reset_token_lifecycle
checkConstraints.expression: (status_code = 'PENDING' AND consumed_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL AND revoked_by IS NULL AND revocation_reason_code IS NULL) OR (status_code = 'CONSUMED' AND consumed_at IS NOT NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL AND revoked_by IS NULL AND revocation_reason_code IS NULL) OR (status_code = 'REVOKED' AND consumed_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NOT NULL AND revoked_by IS NOT NULL AND revocation_reason_code IS NOT NULL) OR (status_code = 'EXPIRED' AND consumed_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL AND revoked_by IS NULL AND revocation_reason_code IS NULL)

checkConstraints.name: chk_pp_t_password_reset_token_attempts

tables.deletePolicy: Revoke or consume immediately; purge only after the configured recovery-security retention period.
securityRules: Reset requests always return the same external response regardless of account existence.
The selector and secret are generated with a cryptographically secure random generator and stored only as keyed hashes.
Changing an email or phone clears its matching verification timestamp in the same transaction; a reset flow never uses an unverified channel.
Token consumption locks the row, verifies PENDING status and expiry, compares the hash in constant time, and transitions exactly once.

Issuance and verification are rate-limited; reset tokens and hashes are never logged.
businessRules: At most one PENDING reset token exists per identity account; issuing a new token first revokes or expires the prior token transactionally.

A token becomes invalid when pp_m_identity_account.credentials_changed_at no longer equals credentials_changed_at_snapshot.
Expired PENDING rows are transitioned lazily on access and by a scheduled cleanup job.

tables.deletePolicy: Application roles have no UPDATE or DELETE privilege. Retention is executed by a controlled archival process.
securityRules: Never store password hashes, tokens, card data, or unnecessary sensitive PII in before_data, after_data, or metadata.
Audit writes should survive mutable entity deletion and therefore intentionally have no foreign keys.
Hash chaining is optional tamper evidence and does not replace restricted database access or external immutable storage.
businessRules: Record authentication events, authorization denials, role changes, customer consent changes, stock adjustments, and order state changes.
Human actor events capture both identity_account_id and the acting business profile in actor_id.
Audit event creation participates in the business transaction when loss is unacceptable.
High-volume read events go to observability logs unless regulatory policy requires database audit.

crossTableBusinessRules.rule: All related organization-owned rows must have the same organization_id.

No organization-wide default shop is inferred. Shop-scoped operations require an explicit trusted selector or derive shop ownership from a server-owned resource, and the resulting shop must be active and belong to the resolved organization.
enforcement: tenant resolver validates explicit organization_id plus shop_id
TenantContext.requireSelectedShopId fails closed for missing shop context
tenant-safe composite foreign keys and repository predicates
unit and integration tests for missing and cross-organization shop selectors

crossTableBusinessRules.rule: A role assignment scope_type must equal its role scope_type.
enforcement: composite foreign key from assignment role_id plus scope_type to role role_id plus scope_type
authorization service validation for clear error responses

crossTableBusinessRules.rule: SHOP scope contains one shop; ORGANIZATION scope contains every shop in that organization; PLATFORM scope contains every organization.
An organization-custom staff or customer role may be assigned only inside the organization that owns the role; system roles with organization_id null follow their declared scope.
enforcement: database trigger only if direct database writes cannot be prohibited

crossTableBusinessRules.rule: is_active = false represents explicit revocation and requires revoked_at, revoked_by, and revoked_reason; natural expiration is determined only from valid_until.
enforcement: staff and customer assignment check constraints

crossTableBusinessRules.rule: Active assignments for the same profile, role, and concrete scope may not have overlapping [valid_from, valid_until) windows, but a new assignment may start exactly when an earlier assignment ends.

Every authentication session and password-reset token belongs to exactly one pp_m_identity_account. A session additionally binds one selected business profile, but credentials and session lifecycle remain identity-owned.
A refresh operation requires an ACTIVE identity account, session, and token family, an unchanged identity credential timestamp, and an atomic current-generation token rotation.
enforcement: row lock or optimistic version comparison

crossTableBusinessRules.rule: Password change, password reset, identity suspension, and detected refresh-token reuse revoke all active sessions and token families for the affected identity account.
Login attempts are append-only and contain a typed, keyed canonical identifier hash rather than submitted usernames, emails, phone numbers, passwords, or bearer tokens.
Every authentication session binds exactly one platform-staff, organization-staff, or customer profile owned by its identity; refresh preserves that profile and cannot switch actor type.
enforcement: organization and shop composite foreign keys
session and JWT profile-claim integration tests

crossTableBusinessRules.rule: Each identity owns at least one optional global username, email, or phone identifier. Every supplied identifier is normalized, globally unique, and never duplicated in staff or customer profile tables.
enforcement: pp_m_identity_account identifier-presence, normalized-pair, and verification check constraints
pp_m_identity_account normalized username, email, and phone unique constraints
username, email, and phone format validation

crossTableBusinessRules.rule: An ACTIVE identity has a verified email or phone. Active platform and organization staff profiles require verified email; active customer profiles require verified email or phone.
enforcement: single transactional identity and profile activation service

crossTableBusinessRules.rule: Every typed login identifier and trusted source-IP uses keyed hashes and row-locked mutable throttle state independently from append-only login history.
enforcement: pp_t_login_throttle_state unique scope and identifier hash
idempotent insert followed by SELECT FOR UPDATE
concurrent threshold and reset integration tests

crossTableBusinessRules.rule: Authentication establishes an identity; authorization requires an active profile owned by that identity, and roles are assigned to profiles rather than directly to identity accounts.
A global customer profile has at most one organization profile per organization and at most one shop profile per shop.
Customer addresses are owned by one global customer profile and at most one ACTIVE address is default at any time.
A shop can sell only products owned by the shop's organization.
A product may reference only a category and optional brand owned by the same organization.
The v2 compatibility status is derived from identity and selected profile lifecycle state; legacy DELETED values are mapped explicitly to ARCHIVED and never silently coerced.
Order totals, price snapshots, stock reservation, cart transition, and order creation are server-controlled and transactional.
Order, payment, and fulfillment status codes are system-managed reference data, while allowed transitions remain code-defined business behavior.
enforcement: Java string enums or explicit code converters

crossTableBusinessRules.rule: Organizations, shops, identity accounts, business profiles, roles, products, offers, and orders are lifecycle-managed rather than physically deleted after use.

requiredApplicationConfiguration.securityRule: Mappings are server-controlled deployment configuration. Do not accept domain mappings from request headers or payloads.

criticalQueryPatterns.name: resolve_login_context
criticalQueryPatterns.description: Classify and resolve one generic global login identifier, then verify the requested active business profile without exposing whether an unrelated identity exists.
contextRules: PLATFORM_STAFF resolves global identity username or email and requires an active platform staff profile with verified identity email.
ORGANIZATION_STAFF resolves global identity username or email plus organization and requires one active organization staff profile with verified identity email.
CUSTOMER resolves verified email or phone and requires an active customer profile. Username is accepted only by an explicitly designated compatibility endpoint.
mandatoryPredicates: submitted identifier is validated, classified, normalized, and HMACed exactly once before throttle or lookup
identifier type is permitted by the requested login context and endpoint policy
submitted identifier matches exactly one normalized identity identifier
staff profiles require identity email_verified_at IS NOT NULL; customer profile requires the selected email or phone channel to be verified
criticalQueryPatterns.privacyRule: External responses and timing do not reveal whether the identity exists but lacks the requested profile.

criticalQueryPatterns.name: enforce_login_throttle
criticalQueryPatterns.description: Evaluate and atomically update canonical typed login-identifier and trusted source-IP throttle state before credential verification.
mandatoryPredicates: scope_code and keyed identifier_hash select one throttle row
locked_until IS NULL OR locked_until <= :now before authentication proceeds
raw login identifiers and source IP are never persisted in throttle rows; login attempts retain only the typed identifier HMAC and trusted source IP under restricted access
criticalQueryPatterns.concurrencyRule: Insert the state idempotently, lock it with SELECT FOR UPDATE, and update the failure window, counter, and lock timestamp in one transaction.
criticalQueryPatterns.privacyRule: Unknown identities and known identities follow the same throttle key derivation and external failure response.

criticalQueryPatterns.name: validate_auth_session
criticalQueryPatterns.description: Validate a server-side session, owning identity, bound profile, and selected tenant context before issuing or accepting refreshed credentials.
mandatoryPredicates: current time is before idle_expires_at and absolute_expires_at
exactly one session-bound profile belongs to identity_account_id and remains ACTIVE
organization and shop context remain valid for the bound profile type
access-token profile claims equal the stored session profile context

criticalQueryPatterns.name: rotate_refresh_token
criticalQueryPatterns.description: Locate a refresh family by keyed selector hash and rotate the current token exactly once.
mandatoryPredicates: current time is before family and session expiry
criticalQueryPatterns.concurrencyRule: Lock the family row with SELECT FOR UPDATE or update with version/current_generation compare-and-swap; rotate hash and generation in the same transaction.

criticalQueryPatterns.name: consume_password_reset_token
criticalQueryPatterns.description: Consume one password-reset token and invalidate all existing credentials for its identity account.
criticalQueryPatterns.concurrencyRule: Lock the reset-token row; consume it, update pp_m_identity_account password_hash and credentials_changed_at, and revoke sessions/families in one transaction.

criticalQueryPatterns.name: effective_platform_staff_assignments
criticalQueryPatterns.description: Load active, currently valid role assignments for one active platform staff profile using the platform-specific repository path.
mandatoryPredicates: identity, profile, role, and permission are active
assignment scope contains the requested organization and shop
criticalQueryPatterns.performanceRule: Verify use of idx_pp_t_staff_role_assignment_platform_active with EXPLAIN ANALYZE and production-like assignment history.

criticalQueryPatterns.name: effective_organization_staff_assignments
criticalQueryPatterns.description: Load active, currently valid role assignments for one active organization staff profile using the tenant-specific repository path.
mandatoryPredicates: identity, profile, role, and permission are active
assignment scope contains the requested shop
criticalQueryPatterns.performanceRule: Verify use of idx_pp_t_staff_role_assignment_org_staff_active with EXPLAIN ANALYZE and production-like tenant history.

criticalQueryPatterns.name: effective_customer_assignments
criticalQueryPatterns.description: Load active, currently valid customer role assignments for one organization customer profile.
mandatoryPredicates: identity, global customer profile, organization profile, role, and permission are active
assignment scope contains the requested shop
criticalQueryPatterns.performanceRule: Verify use of idx_pp_t_customer_role_assignment_profile_active with EXPLAIN ANALYZE and production-like tenant history.

criticalQueryPatterns.name: account_directory_by_username_or_status
criticalQueryPatterns.description: Build the v2 compatibility user-directory projection without recreating a generic user aggregate.
mandatoryPredicates: non-platform queries include organization_id from trusted tenant context
status filtering applies the documented effective identity/profile status
only currently effective role assignments are returned
customer addresses are returned only for the owning customer profile
criticalQueryPatterns.performanceRule: Use a bounded projection query or two-phase paginated ID query plus batched associations; never page over a multi-collection fetch join.
criticalQueryPatterns.compatibilityRule: The projection preserves username, organization, active roles and assignments, effective status, address list, and audit metadata while exposing UUID identifiers.

criticalQueryPatterns.name: customer_addresses
criticalQueryPatterns.description: List, create, or retrieve addresses owned by the authenticated global customer profile.
criticalQueryPatterns.concurrencyRule: Changing the default clears the current default and sets the new default in one transaction; the partial unique index rejects concurrent dual defaults.

criticalQueryPatterns.name: users_in_shop
criticalQueryPatterns.description: Return active organization staff profiles whose active identities have a SHOP assignment for the requested shop, plus organization-scoped profiles when inherited access is requested.
mandatoryPredicates: assignment is active and currently valid
identity, staff profile, and role are active

criticalQueryPatterns.name: nearby_shops
criticalQueryPatterns.description: Return active shops ordered by distance from the customer's current coordinates.
criticalQueryPatterns.implementation: Use a latitude/longitude bounding-box prefilter plus Haversine calculation for initial scale; migrate to PostGIS ST_DWithin and ST_Distance with a GiST geography index for large datasets.
criticalQueryPatterns.privacyRule: Location permission is optional, purpose-limited, and not stored unless the customer explicitly opts in.

criticalQueryPatterns.name: favorite_shops
criticalQueryPatterns.description: Return active favorite shops for a customer across organization profiles.

criticalQueryPatterns.name: category_subtree
criticalQueryPatterns.description: Return one organization-owned category and all descendants while guarding against invalid cycles.
mandatoryPredicates: organization_id = :organizationId in both anchor and recursive terms
a visited UUID path prevents repeated traversal
criticalQueryPatterns.performanceRule: Index organization_id plus parent_product_category_id and enforce a configured maximum hierarchy depth in the service.

criticalQueryPatterns.name: products_by_category_subtree
criticalQueryPatterns.description: Return paginated organization products for a category subtree with optional brand summary and stable sorting.
mandatoryPredicates: product_category_id is in the tenant-constrained category subtree
brand is null or belongs to the same organization
ordinary customer catalog reads include only permitted lifecycle states
criticalQueryPatterns.performanceRule: Page products before mapping related category and brand summaries; validate API sort aliases against explicit columns.

criticalQueryPatterns.name: standalone_explicit_shop_catalog
criticalQueryPatterns.description: Resolve the configured organization and an explicitly selected active shop, then return active products through that shop's active offers. Missing shop context is rejected rather than replaced.
mandatoryPredicates: the selected shop is active and belongs to the configured organization
ordinary customer catalog reads include only active offers and permitted product lifecycle states

schemaManagement: Translate the approved model into small, ordered Liquibase changesets.
Implement all 38 core tables in the documented creation order; pp_t_login_throttle_state, pp_m_customer_address, and pp_m_brand are required by the current-functionality parity baseline.
Install the PostgreSQL btree_gist extension in a controlled prerequisite changeset before creating temporal role-assignment exclusion constraints.

Create and seed pp_m_order_status, pp_m_payment_status, and pp_m_fulfillment_status before creating pp_t_order and its status foreign keys; use idempotent, version-controlled reference-data changesets.
Set spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate outside disposable local tests.
Run Liquibase validation and migration tests against a real PostgreSQL instance.
Generate the physical ERD from the migrated database, not manually from this JSON.

migrationDecision.noProductionData: Create a new v2 baseline and rebuild the disposable database after backing up any useful development seed data.
migrationDecision.productionOrValuableData: Use expand-migrate-contract changesets with backfill, dual-read or dual-write only where necessary, reconciliation queries, and a tested rollback plan.

identityMigration: Create one identity account for each existing credential record by default; never merge records solely because email or phone values match.
Move every provided legacy username, email, and phone to pp_m_identity_account; normalize each channel and fail seed generation on duplicate normalized identifiers.
Create PENDING identities or profiles when a required verified channel cannot be proven. Do not manufacture verification timestamps during a migration.
Link profiles to one identity only after verified ownership, an authenticated session, or an approved administrative reconciliation workflow.
Backfill profile foreign keys and reconcile global identifier conflicts before enforcing unique constraints.
Map legacy BUYER accounts to customer profiles and customer roles; map SELLER and ADMIN accounts to explicitly approved organization-staff role equivalents.

Create a customer profile for every legacy identity that owns saved addresses, including identities that also receive a staff profile; preserve ADDRESS_MANAGE self-service authorization where current behavior requires it.
Map legacy DELETED lifecycle values to ARCHIVED through an explicit seed mapping.
Revoke legacy sessions and password-reset tokens at credential-root cutover unless a formally verified token migration exists.
referenceDataMigration: Insert every canonical status row before adding or validating pp_t_order status foreign keys.
Reconcile existing order status values against an explicit migration mapping; fail the migration on unknown values instead of silently coercing them.
Deploy application enum or converter support before any new status code can be written.

Use expand-and-contract deployment ordering when adding a future status: seed database reference data first, deploy readers and writers second, and deprecate old codes only after all writers stop producing them.
security: Use least-privilege database roles for migration, application read/write, reporting, and audit archival.
Encrypt database storage and backups; use TLS for database connections.
Mask PII in logs and non-production datasets.
Store refresh/reset token HMAC keys in a managed secret store, support key versioning and rotation, and never expose them as ordinary application configuration values.
Use cryptographically secure random bearer tokens, constant-time hash comparison, refresh-token rotation, reuse detection, and transactional session revocation.

Return enumeration-safe login and password-reset responses, classify generic identifiers consistently, and enforce distributed identifier and source-IP rate limits through the core pp_t_login_throttle_state table.
Bind access-token profile claims to the profile context stored in pp_t_auth_session and reject any profile or tenant mismatch.
Tenant administrators operate on organization profiles and invitations; they cannot directly search or mutate unrelated pp_m_identity_account rows.
Role assignments are created and revoked only through the transactional authorization service; ordinary application paths do not expose unrestricted assignment repositories.
Canonical order, payment, and fulfillment status catalogs have no tenant-admin CRUD API and are writable only by the migration role.
Validate uploaded image content and never trust a client-provided MIME type.
Apply OWASP authentication, session, access-control, and input-validation guidance.

Schema constraint tests for every unique, check, and foreign-key rule.
Cross-tenant isolation integration tests for every organization-owned repository.
Authorization matrix tests covering identity, active profile, permission, role, and scope.
Role-assignment constraint tests rejecting profile-type mismatch, role-scope mismatch, organization-staff PLATFORM scope, cross-tenant profile/shop references, and duplicate active assignments.
Assignment lifecycle tests proving that natural expiry remains active-but-ineffective and explicit revocation requires complete revocation metadata.
Temporal-assignment concurrency tests rejecting overlapping effective windows while allowing adjacent and otherwise non-overlapping reassignment windows.
Custom-role ownership tests proving that organization-owned staff and customer roles cannot be assigned outside their owning organization.
Profile-isolation tests proving that disabling one organization membership does not disable another staff membership or customer profile.
Account-linking tests proving that matching email or phone values never merge identities without ownership verification.

Identity-identifier tests covering optional identifier pairs, at-least-one presence, normalized username/email/phone uniqueness, format, concurrent registration, verification reset after contact change, and enumeration-safe lookup.

Authentication tests covering context-allowed identifier channels, unknown-account timing, lockout, verified-contact profile activation, session idle/absolute expiry, credential-change invalidation, logout, and concurrent refresh.
Session-context tests proving identity/profile ownership, profile-type exclusivity, organization/shop consistency, and refresh-context immutability.
Login-throttle concurrency tests proving idempotent initialization, row-locked threshold updates, expiry-window reset, and keyed identifier redaction.
Refresh-token replay tests proving that stale-token reuse atomically compromises the family and revokes the parent session.
Password-reset tests covering enumeration resistance, expiry, single use, concurrent consumption, prior-token replacement, and session revocation.
Login-attempt tests covering redaction, append-only privileges, trusted-proxy IP resolution, partition retention, and failure-path recording.
Customer-address tests covering ownership, first-address defaulting, concurrent default changes, archival, and order snapshot independence.
Catalog parity tests covering tenant-safe category recursion, cycle protection, brand ownership, model-number mapping, pagination, and stable sort aliases.
Current API parity contract tests for login, refresh, logout, registration, account lookup, status pagination, customer addresses, category details, and products by category subtree.
Concurrent cart update, checkout idempotency, and stock reservation tests.
Reference-data tests proving every application status code is seeded exactly once, deprecated rows remain referentially valid, and unknown order status codes are rejected by foreign keys.
Order state-machine tests covering every allowed and forbidden order, payment, and fulfillment transition, including concurrent updates.
Order snapshot and money-rounding tests.
Audit redaction and immutability tests.
performance: Verify indexes with EXPLAIN ANALYZE using production-like tenant sizes.
Avoid fetching permissions separately per request; cache immutable permission catalogs and invalidate on role changes.
Use separate platform-staff, organization-staff, and customer assignment repository queries so each query matches its active partial index and avoids nullable-branch OR predicates.
Avoid N+1 role-permission loading; fetch effective role and permission codes in a bounded query or use an invalidation-aware role-permission cache.

Map order status columns as scalar string enums or code value objects; cache the small reference catalogs for presentation metadata and do not add eager JPA many-to-one associations to transactional orders.

Retain B-tree active lookup indexes even though GiST exclusion constraints create backing indexes; exclusion indexes enforce overlap integrity and are not assumed to optimize ordinary authorization lookups.
Do not update auth-session last_seen_at on every request; use a bounded write interval while enforcing expiry from authoritative timestamps.
Partition login attempts only after measured volume justifies it, and keep low-latency throttling state separate from append-only history.
Use the throttle-state scope and identifier unique index for point lookups and the locked-until partial index only for operational cleanup and monitoring.
Use the customer-address owner index for ordered reads and rely on the partial unique index, not application reads alone, for default-address concurrency.
Paginate all shop, product, customer, order, and audit queries using stable sort keys.
Partition audit data when volume and retention requirements justify it.
Use PostGIS only when nearby-shop volume requires spatial indexing.
